title: Projective model structures on complex-enriched diagrams and cofibrant evaluation
statement:
Use the dg-category, cochain-complex and model-category conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], in sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal N$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$. Here enrichment means unital associative composition chain maps on complexes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)$ whose degree-zero cycles are the ordinary morphisms. Tensors $K\otimes X$ and cotensors $Y^K$ satisfy the natural complex adjunctions $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(K\otimes X,Y)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y^K)$. Locally presentable means that, for some regular cardinal $\kappa$, a set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits generates all objects under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Suppose it has a cofibrantly generated model structure and satisfies the enriched model axiom: for a cofibration $i:P\to Q$ and a fibration $p:X\to Y$, the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Y)$$
is a degreewise surjection of complexes, and is a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ is a weak equivalence. An object is cofibrant if its initial map is a cofibration, and fibrant if its terminal map is a fibration. Assume a set $I$ of generating cofibrations has cofibrant domains and codomains, and write $J$ for a set of generating trivial cofibrations. Generating means that the maps having the right lifting property against $I$, respectively $J$, are precisely the trivial fibrations, respectively fibrations. Assume also the tensor-cell acyclicity condition: let $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N}$ be the smallest class of arrows containing every $K\otimes j$, for every complex $K$ and every trivial cofibration $j$ of $\mathcal N$, and all isomorphisms, and closed under small coproducts, pushouts, transfinite compositions continuous at limit ordinals, and retracts in the arrow category; every arrow of $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N}$ is a weak equivalence. A retract in the arrow category means a retract through commutative squares. This is the tensor-action version of the monoid acyclicity condition, with retract closure made explicit. For every small dg category $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbf Z$, the category $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$ of strict complex-enriched functors and enriched natural transformations has the projective cofibrantly generated model structure: weak equivalences and fibrations are detected at each object of $\mathcal C$, and cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial fibrations. It is again complete, cocomplete and locally presentable, enriched, tensored and cotensored over complexes, and satisfies the displayed enriched model axiom for its actual complexes of enriched natural transformations. For functors $F,G$, degree $r$ of this complex consists of families $\eta_c\in\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(F(c),G(c))^r$ satisfying $G(a)\eta_c=(-1)^{r|a|}\eta_{c'}F(a)$ for every homogeneous $a\in\mathcal C(c,c')$; the differential and composition are componentwise. The generating maps are $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes i$ for $c\in\mathcal C$ and $i\in I$, and $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes j$ for $j\in J$; the former have cofibrant domains and codomains in $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$. The tensor-cell acyclicity condition also holds in $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$ for its pointwise complex tensor. If every object of $\mathcal N$ is fibrant, the same is true in $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$.

If every $\mathcal C(c,c')$ is cofibrant in the projective model structure on complexes, evaluation at every $c$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, hence sends cofibrant diagrams to cofibrant objects. Here $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes P$ is the enriched free diagram whose value at $c'$ is $\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes P$, left adjoint to evaluation at $c$.

The category $\mathcal N=\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ with weak equivalences the quasi-isomorphisms, fibrations the degreewise surjections and cofibrations defined by lifting satisfies all the hypotheses above, and all its objects are fibrant. Its generating cofibrations may be taken as $S^{n+1}\to D^n$ and its generating trivial cofibrations as $0\to D^n$, for all $n\in\mathbf Z$, where $S^{n+1}$ is $\mathbf Z$ in degree $n+1$ and zero elsewhere, and $D^n$ is $\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{1}\mathbf Z$ in degrees $n,n+1$; the sphere-to-disk map is the identity in degree $n+1$ and zero in every other degree.

external.document: Bertrand Toën, The homotopy theory of dg-categories and derived Morita theory, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337
external.place: Section 3, Definition 3.1 and the model-structure paragraphs before Proposition 3.2, Proposition 3.3 and its proof; the projective complex model structure in Section 2; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For strict dg functors $F,G$, form the subcomplex of $\prod_c\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(F(c),G(c))$ cut out in degree $r$ by $G(a)\eta_c=(-1)^{r|a|}\eta_{c'}F(a)$. Applying the differential to this equation and using the chain-map composition rule gives the same equation for $d\eta$ in degree $r+1$; composing equations of degrees $r,s$ gives the equation of degree $r+s$. Thus componentwise differential, composition and identity give exactly the claimed enrichment. Give $K\otimes F$ its pointwise tensor values, moving $K$ past each source morphism with the Koszul symmetry before the action, and give $G^K$ the transposed action. The complex tensor-Hom adjunction in $\mathcal N$, applied at every object, identifies their families satisfying these equations, so supplies the complex tensor and cotensor adjunctions for diagrams. Limits have the componentwise limit values, with actions transposed through the cotensor adjunction; colimits have componentwise colimit values, since each $L\otimes-$ is a left adjoint and preserves colimits. Their universal properties, and the action identities, are checked on the limiting projections or colimit legs. These constructions require only small products/equalizers of complexes and the given tensors and cotensors.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: explicit strict enriched diagram objects and mapping complexes, before the finite adjunction comparison.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and define $T$ on $\mathcal N^S$ by $(TX)_{c'}=\coprod_{c\in S}\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes X_c$. Units in $\mathcal C$ define $\eta$, and its composition maps define $\mu$ on the summands of $T^2X$; the two monad identities are precisely the unit and associativity identities of $\mathcal C$. A structure map $TX\to X$ is exactly the family of dg action maps, and its algebra equations are exactly the strict-functor equations. Thus strict dg diagrams and $T$-algebras are identical categories over $\mathcal N^S$. Every tensor $\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes-$ and every small coproduct preserves colimits, so $T$ preserves all small colimits and hence $\lambda$-filtered colimits for any infinite regular $\lambda$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability] to the product of copies of $\mathcal N$ indexed by $S$ to conclude that the diagram category is locally presentable. Its completeness and cocompleteness are the explicit constructions of step 1. The cardinal used for the algebra category may be enlarged; the argument never assumes it equals the original presentability cardinal of $\mathcal N$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: local presentability needed for the enriched small-object construction; accessible-monad foundation, Adamek-Rosicky Corollary 1.54 and Theorem 2.78.

proof.text: For $c\in\mathcal C$ define $F_cP(c')=\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes P$, with action given by composition. Restricting a transformation $F_cP\to H$ along $1_c$ gives a map $P\to H(c)$; conversely extend that map by the action of every $\mathcal C(c,c')$. The unit and associativity equations make these inverse, naturally. The same formula for a homogeneous degree-$r$ map has the sign $(-1)^{r|a|}$ when extended along a homogeneous $a$, so this is an adjunction of actual Hom complexes, not just ordinary Hom sets. In particular $F_c$ preserves colimits. Set $I_{\mathcal C}=\{F_ci:c\in\mathcal C,i\in I\}$ and $J_{\mathcal C}=\{F_cj:c\in\mathcal C,j\in J\}$. These are sets because the object set and generating families are small. Transposing each lifting square gives $I_{\mathcal C}^{\square}=$ objectwise trivial fibrations and $J_{\mathcal C}^{\square}=$ objectwise fibrations, by the two generating hypotheses in the item.

source.place: Toën, Section 3, representables before Definition 3.1 and generating maps in the proof of Proposition 3.2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] in the locally presentable category from step 2, once with $I_{\mathcal C}$ and once with $J_{\mathcal C}$. Every map therefore factors as a relative cell map for the indicated set followed by a map in its right lifting class. A cell map has the left lifting property against that class: choose the specified fillers on each attached summand, extend across each pushout at a successor, and use the colimit universal property at each limit. If $f$ has that left lifting property and $f=pj$ is the cell factorization, lift in the square with left edge $f$ and right edge $p$ to exhibit $f$ as a retract of $j$ in the arrow category. Consequently the two left classes are exactly the retracts of the respective relative cell maps. Use also [lem-coef-presentable-small-object-factorization], with the same two generating sets, to choose functorial factorizations in these left/right classes. This separates the functorial assertion from the cellular assertion: neither cited statement is being read as claiming the other's extra conclusion.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: the two locally presentable small-object factorizations; explicit transfinite lifting and retract argument.

proof.text: Let $W,F$ denote objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, put $C={}^{\square}(F\cap W)$ and $L={}^{\square}F$. Evaluating a $J_{\mathcal C}$-cell attachment at $d$ gives a pushout of a coproduct of maps $\mathcal C(c,d)\otimes j$. Evaluation preserves all colimits by step 1. Therefore every such relative cell map is objectwise in $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N}$, hence in $W$ by the corrected tensor-cell hypothesis. Every map of $L$ is a retract of such a map by step 4, so $L\subset W$. Also $L\subset C$, since $F\cap W\subset F$. Conversely, for $f\in C\cap W$, factor $f=pj$ with $j$ a $J_{\mathcal C}$-cell map and $p\in F$. We have $j\in W$, hence $p\in F\cap W$ by two-out-of-three. The lifting property of $f$ against $p$ exhibits $f$ as a retract of $j$, so $f\in L$. Thus $L=C\cap W$. Step 4 and the lifting identifications of step 3 give the two weak factorization systems $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$. The classes are retract closed, and $W$ has two-out-of-three componentwise. These are precisely the model axioms in the conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], proving the projective model structure and the asserted generators.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: right transfer verified from both weak factorization systems, with the missing tensor-cell acyclicity made explicit.

proof.text: First transpose lifting squares through the given tensor-Hom adjunction in $\mathcal N$. If $k$ is a cofibration of complexes and $i$ a cofibration of $\mathcal N$, then $k\mathbin{\square}i$ lifts against every trivial fibration: the transposed problem is a lift of $k$ against the trivial fibration of complexes in the displayed enriched model axiom. If $k$ or $i$ is trivial it lifts against every fibration, by the same axiom. Here $k\mathbin{\square}i$ is $(B\otimes P)\amalg_{A\otimes P}(A\otimes Q)\to B\otimes Q$ for $k:A\to B$ and $i:P\to Q$. Thus it is a cofibration, trivial in these two cases. In diagrams, $k\mathbin{\square}F_ci=F_c(k\mathbin{\square}i)$ by the tensor symmetry and step 1. Since evaluation preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations, its left adjoint $F_c$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, by transposing lifts. By step 4 every diagram cofibration is a retract of an $I_{\mathcal C}$-cell map, and every trivial one a retract of a $J_{\mathcal C}$-cell map. Tensor and pushout product preserve the attaching colimits and retracts. More explicitly, if $X=X_0\to X_\theta=Y$ is a cell presentation and $k:A\to B$, filter its pushout product by $T_\alpha=(B\otimes X_\alpha)\amalg_{A\otimes X_\alpha}(A\otimes Y)$. The first term is the domain of $k\mathbin{\square}(X\to Y)$ and the last is $B\otimes Y$. If $X_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$ attaches $P\to Q$, expansion of the two pushouts identifies $T_\alpha\to T_{\alpha+1}$ with a pushout of $(B\otimes P)\amalg_{A\otimes P}(A\otimes Q)\to B\otimes Q$. At limits the equality follows because both tensors preserve colimits. Thus the transfinite lifting construction of step 4 applies to this filtration, and then to its retracts. Extending the generator calculation along these presentations proves the same pushout-product assertions for every diagram cofibration. Finally transpose again using the actual Hom complex of step 1. For a diagram cofibration $i$ and fibration $p$, the relative Hom map lifts against every generating trivial cofibration of complexes; if either $i$ or $p$ is trivial, it lifts against every generating cofibration. By [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] at $R=\mathbf Z$, this says exactly degreewise surjectivity and, in the latter cases, quasi-isomorphism. This proves the enriched model axiom without claiming that an arbitrary limit of surjective Hom maps is surjective.

source.place: Toën, Section 3, model-structure paragraphs after Definition 3.1; explicit pushout-product/lifting proof of compatibility.

proof.text: Step 6 already shows that $F_c$ is left Quillen. If $P$ is a domain or codomain of a generator in $I$, $0\to P$ is a cofibration by hypothesis; applying $F_c$ shows $F_cP$ cofibrant. This proves cofibrancy of both endpoints of every generator in $I_{\mathcal C}$, without requiring $\mathcal C(c,c')$ to be cofibrant. If every object of $\mathcal N$ is fibrant, the component maps of any diagram to the terminal diagram are fibrations, and so every diagram is fibrant. Both assertions use the projective lifting classes proved in step 5.

source.place: Toën, Section 3, proof of Proposition 3.2: free generating objects; objectwise definition of fibrations.

proof.text: Now assume every $\mathcal C(c,d)$ is cofibrant in complexes. For any cofibration $i$ of $\mathcal N$, the map $\mathcal C(c,d)\otimes i$ is $(0\to\mathcal C(c,d))\mathbin{\square}i$, hence a cofibration by step 6, trivial if $i$ is trivial. Evaluation at $d$ sends generators in $I_{\mathcal C}$ to these cofibrations, and generators in $J_{\mathcal C}$ to trivial cofibrations. It preserves coproducts, pushouts, continuous transfinite compositions and retracts. The retract-of-cell presentations of step 4, and the transfinite lifting construction there for the lifting classes of $\mathcal N$, therefore show that it preserves all cofibrations and all trivial cofibrations. Its preservation of the initial diagram now sends cofibrant diagrams to cofibrant objects. No flatness or cofibrancy of source morphism complexes was used in steps 1-7; precisely this additional evaluation conclusion requires it.

source.place: Toën, Proposition 3.3 and its proof, pp. 14-15 (PDF pp. 14-15 in the displayed numbering).

proof.text: The corrected tensor-cell hypothesis is inherited, so the theorem can still be iterated for module diagrams. Fix $K$ and a diagram trivial cofibration $u$. By step 4 it is a retract of a $J_{\mathcal C}$-cell map. Tensoring with $K$ preserves its cellular presentation and retract. After evaluating at $d$, each attached generating map is $(K\otimes\mathcal C(c,d))\otimes j$, an element of $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N}$. Thus every $(K\otimes u)(d)$ belongs to $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N}$. The class of diagram arrows whose values all belong to $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N}$ contains these tensor maps and all isomorphisms, and is closed under coproducts, pushouts, continuous transfinite compositions and retracts, since these are componentwise. It therefore contains the class $\mathscr A_{\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}}$ defined by the corrected hypothesis. Every such map is objectwise a weak equivalence, as required. This argument uses the saturated class in the hypothesis; it does not assert closure of arbitrary weak equivalences under pushouts or transfinite composition.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: acyclicity for iterated projective module diagram models, by evaluation of tensor cells.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] with $R=\mathbf Z$. It supplies completeness, cocompleteness, local presentability, both generating sets, the projective weak equivalences and fibrations, and the closed symmetric monoidal pushout-product axiom. Its closed structure is exactly enrichment, tensor and cotensor over complexes; transposing its pushout-product lifting property as in step 6 proves the displayed enriched model axiom. The terminal map of every complex is degreewise surjective, so every complex is fibrant. The generating spheres and disks have projective terms: Hom from a sphere is a shift of the target, and Hom from a disk is contractible. Thus these complexes are dg-projective and hence cofibrant by the node's characterization of cofibrations; this verifies both generating endpoints. Finally verify the added tensor-cell condition. A trivial cofibration $j:P\to Q$ has a chain retraction by lifting against the fibration $P\to0$. Hence $Q=P\oplus E$ as complexes. Its cokernel $E$ is acyclic and dg-projective by the cited characterization. Applying the definition of dg-projectivity to $E$ itself makes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(E,E)$ acyclic, so $1_E=dh+hd$ for a degree-$-1$ map $h$; $E$ is contractible. For arbitrary $K$, the map $K\otimes j$ is the split inclusion with contractible cokernel $K\otimes E$, contracted by $k\otimes e\mapsto(-1)^{|k|}k\otimes h(e)$. Split inclusions with contractible cokernel are closed under small coproducts and pushouts. For a continuous transfinite composite, choose a chain splitting at each successor: recursively the colimit is the initial complex plus the direct sum of the successor cokernels, contracted componentwise. Retracts remain split inclusions and their cokernels are retracts of contractible complexes, with contracting homotopy obtained by inclusion, contraction and projection. Thus this class is closed under every operation defining $\mathscr A$, and every map in it is a chain homotopy equivalence, in particular a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the added hypothesis for $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ and completes all clauses.

source.place: Toën, conventions before Section 2 and Section 3; existing projective cochain model, with explicit tensor-cell contraction calculation.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2: strict projective dg diagram infrastructure for the finite mapping comparison. Toën Section 3 motivates the route; the transfer, pushout-product and tensor-cell arguments are written explicitly because its blanket projective-existence assertion omits an acyclicity hypothesis.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: arbitrary dg model targets do not admit objectwise-fibration projective diagram models without tensor-cell acyclicity; the injective model on Ch(Z), indexed by the dg algebra Z/p, is a counterexample. Added the explicit saturated tensor-cell acyclicity hypothesis and proved its inheritance and its validity for the intended projective complex models. Constructed strict enriched diagrams and their free actions, used the existing accessible-monad presentability statement lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability (the proposed new monad node was a duplicate and was removed) and the existing small-object statements, proved both weak factorization systems and enriched compatibility, and gave the evaluation and concrete generators arguments. No Lean attachment, no compiler, no SGA source.

Statement correction (E7): checked independently and holds. The injective model on Ch(Z) satisfies Hovey's enriched axiom, since k□i is a mono whose cokernel is a shift or a contractible disk tensor. For the one-object dg category with endomorphisms Z/p, a fibrant diagram would have terms that are both divisible and p-torsion, so every fibrant diagram is zero. The source's blanket existence claim is therefore false. The added saturated tensor-cell acyclicity hypothesis is what the Kan transfer uses. Its inheritance (step 9) and its validity for projective Ch(Z) (step 10) are proved. I checked the Koszul contraction sign, chain-splitting by lifting, and retract closure.
